messages:
Samir Patel: FYI I'm seeing a ~17% drop in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel selector change in canary. Quick dump from profiling attached below.

Samir Patel: key metric: cache_hitrate_global = 0.63 -> 0.52 after deploy. cache_miss_p50_latency up 40ms.

Maya Chen: Oof. Which paths impacted most? small prompts vs long streaming?

Samir Patel: Mostly short prompts (<=64 tokens) and the streaming chat path. Looks like a keying mismatch + some extra entropy introduced by canonicalization changes in the new kernel path.

Lina Gomez: Can you paste an example of the cache key before/after?

Samir Patel: Sure — simplified: 
Before: model:v1|prefix_hash:ab12cd|user_lang:en
After:  model:v1|prefix_hash:ab12cd|session_id:null|user_lang:en
(we accidentally started including session_id when present, which increases cardinality)

Zach Lee: Ah that explains it. Session_id is notoriously high-entropy. We should never include ephemeral session ids in cache keying.

Maya Chen: Besides removing session id, are there other sources of entropy? whitespace normalization? trailing newlines?

Samir Patel: Yep — kernel path started preserving raw input meta (leading/trailing spaces, some zero-width chars). Small diffs in prefix lead to different keys.

Lina Gomez: For a quick rollback: we can push a keying-normalization hotfix that strips session_id and normalizes whitespace. Can we also add a server-side TTL header to reduce blowup? e.g., x-cache-ttl: 30s for ephemeral prefixes.

Samir Patel: Good plan. Also we should add a telemetry tag: cache_key_entropy_bucket so we can surface how many keys have high entropy.

infra-bot: Deployed canary 1837654300 -> kernel-selector v2.2. Added metric: runtime.cache_key_entropy. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/c/keys/1837654321

Zach Lee: SDK-level: we should make opt-in header explicit and fail-safe for retries/streaming. Example header suggestion: 

  X-Redwood-Cache: opt-in
  X-Redwood-Cache-Mode: eager-prefill

Maya Chen: streaming edge case: when client retries mid-stream we lose the prefetched KV because retry didn't include opt-in header (some HTTP clients drop custom headers on redirect/retry). We need SDKs to persist the header and also include it in body-level grpc/stream metadata for streaming transports.

Lina Gomez: For warmup strategies: two options — (1) server-side eager warmup on model route create (cheap prefill for top N prefixes observed in telemetry), (2) client-driven prefill API that SDKs call once on new model pin. Both need to respect opt-in semantics.

Samir Patel: I ran a simulation: normalizing key + stripping session_id + TTL 30s + eager warmup for top-100 prefixes yields predicted hit-rate back to ~0.69 and reduces unique-key growth by ~45%.

Zach Lee: Nice. Action items:
- Samir: PR for key normalization + unit tests (include whitespace, ZWSP cases)
- Maya: SDK patch to persist X-Redwood-Cache header across retries and streaming reconnects
- Lina: telemetry patch: cache_key_entropy_bucket, warmup_success_rate, prefills_per_model
- infra-bot: run canary for 24h and postting windows (p95 latency, cache_hitrate)

Maya Chen: I'll also add an integration test that simulates a streaming client that reconnects mid-response and verifies cache opt-in survives the retry.

Samir Patel: I'll open the PRs now. Putting a short-term mitigation: rollback kernel-selector to v2.1 on canary if canary cache_hitrate < 0.6 after 2h.

Zach Lee: Ping me when PRs are up, I'll review. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary monitor job started (check: runtime.cache_hitrate_global, runtime.p95_latency). Alerts if hit-rate drops >10% for 30m.
